note: Red Linn is within ~1-2 m of the centre of the 1904 50 ft Linn (checked at two cross-sections). OSM Linn runs ~9.6 m west, through the 1904 west-side buildings, so the street was widened or realigned. Neighbouring streets match OSM within 1-2 m, so the sheet is not shifted.
Red Gest is centred in the printed 60 ft band (two spots, within ~1 m). OSM runs along or just inside the 1904 south building line ~8 m south. Hopkins and Dalton are not offset the same way.
The whole flagged stretch of McMicken lies in a no-coverage gap between two sheets. The red line there is a straight interpolation, so it can't be checked.
Red Dalton is centred on the printed 60 ft band (within ~0.5 m near Poplar). OSM is ~3.5 m east of the 1904 centre.
Red York is centred in the printed 50 ft band (two spots, within ~1 m). OSM runs along or north of the 1904 north lot line, ~8 m north.

Nearly all of the flagged stretch (west of Dalton) has no sheet under it. On the ~25 m that is covered, east of Dalton, red is centred in the printed 60 ft band and OSM is ~3 m south, which looks like A1.
Red E 3rd is centred in the 1904 band near Eggleston (three cross-sections, within ~1 m). OSM E 3rd sits ~4 m south-east, in the rebuilt Fort Washington Way corridor.

Red W 9th is centred in the 1904 band (within ~1.5 m). OSM runs 8-12 m north, along and through the 1904 north frontage, because of the modern realignment toward Central. Central and Richmond match OSM.
Red Broadway is centred in the printed 100 ft band, between the rail-yard line and the west frontage. OSM has split carriageways that curve near Mehring.
Red E 4th is centred in the printed 30 ft band, between the Factory/Wood Work frontage and the Frank Tea & Spice frontage. OSM is ~3 m north-west, near the north frontage.
Red Main is within ~1 m of the centre of the ~50 ft band (two cross-sections). OSM is ~2.5-3.5 m west of the 1904 centre.
Red E 3rd is within ~1.5 m of the centre of the printed 60 ft band, between the Anna Louise Inn and the 513-529 frontages. OSM is ~5 m north-west, along the north frontage.
Red Linn is centred on the 1904 Linn, between the Hilda/921-925 and 950/920-934 frontages (profile within ~1 m). OSM Linn is the modern diagonal through the west block.
Red is centred in the ~10 ft Henderson Alley gap (Whol. Tires vs bldg 327; Auto Parking vs Hotel). OSM is ~3.5 m east and passes through 1904 bldg 327.
Red E 5th runs between the two water-pipe lines in the 1904 band, roughly centred. OSM is ~7 m south, on the south frontage, because of the modern realignment at Pike/Sentinel.
Red Broadway is within ~1 m of the centre of the printed 100 ft band, between the west block line and the 236-228 frontage. OSM curves east through the 1904 east block.

The west half of the stretch has no sheet. On the covered part, red is ~2 m south of the centre of the printed 50 ft band (bldg 1244 south face to the south lot line). OSM is 8-10 m north, along the north frontage.
Red Budd is within ~1-2 m of the centre of the printed 50 ft band on both sides of Harriet. OSM is ~2-3 m north of centre west of Harriet and stops at Harriet.
The modern diagonal Gest cuts across many 1904 blocks of houses between Richmond and Barr. There was no street on that line in 1904.
The modern diagonal Linn runs through 1904 house lots from W 8th to below Kenyon/Dalton. The 1904 Linn is the straight N-S street further east.
The modern Elm curve runs through 1904 buildings below W 3rd and across the Cincinnati Southern freight depot to W Water. The 1904 Elm is the red line further west.
The modern W 2nd runs through the Central Union Passenger train shed and the C.C.C.&St.L. freight house. There was no street there in 1904.
A narrow (~10 ft) N-S mid-block alley is visible all along, crossing W Court, Carter Alley and W 9th between Race and Elm. The name and width are illegible.
The modern Monastery runs ~20-25 m north of 1904 Ellen. It cuts through the William J. Morgan Public School block and house lots 332-302, with no street on that line.

to: Branch Street (red stub near Henry St)
note: BRANCH is printed in the street, with 30 ft printed at the north end and house numbers 2042-2008. Our red Branch only covers the short south stub.
An E-W alley runs mid-block between W 9th and W 8th, crossing Moore Alley and Haven Alley, with a water pipe printed in it. The name and width are not legible.
Central Parkway lies on the 1904 Miami Canal bed and tow path. There was no street there.

Only partly covered. The sheet shows a ~25 ft way leaving Vine to the south-east for ~25 m to the sheet edge, and Hurst Alley continuing ~15 m north-west of Lang to the sheet edge. The middle ~40 m has no sheet. Probably a NW extension of red Hurst Alley.

Only 'ALLEY' is printed (no name). It is the east continuation of the Brighton alley, and OSM runs along the north edge of the band. A '10' near the Kimpel Alley junction is ambiguous, so no width is given.
The Derrick Turnbow Ave turnaround loop at Armory/Cutter runs through 1904 house lots on both sides.
The OSM Hammond St E-W leg runs through 1904 buildings and lots (316-312 Main etc.) between Main and Hammond, mid-block between E 4th and E 3rd.
A narrow (~10 ft) N-S passage with a dashed pipe line runs between the Fort Washington/hotel block and the iron-clad building. No name or width is printed, and it could be a private passage (unsure).

Half the stretch is in a no-coverage gap between two sheets, and the two sheets disagree on where Freeman Av is by ~30 m. On each sheet the line falls inside or at the edge of the Freeman Av band, so it is probably the modern Sargent curve merging into Freeman, but the conflicting sheets mean I can't tell.

The modern Eggleston crosses the Armstrong Cork/Woodwork building corner and then the printed 80 ft Lockport Av band at an angle, rather than following any 1904 street. Separate issue: red Lockport Avenue does not follow the printed Lockport band here. It runs up to ~30 m north-east, through the Armstrong Cork buildings, at its north-west end.
A N-S alley with 'ALLEY' printed runs between bldgs 138/136 and 130, crossing Grandin Alley. North of Grandin it continues between Variol Mfg and the Upholst. building. No name or width is printed.
The Partridge Place turnaround circle and its east leg run through the Lammers & Hollmeyer yard and the Meyer Bros factory lot on either side of Linn.
Rusconi Place, from Borden Alley south to W 6th, runs through a narrow yellow (frame) building strip between lots. There was no passage there in 1904.
The modern Linn diagonal runs through 1904 houses (822/824 area).
CUMBER is printed in a narrow street running north from E Liberty to the edge of the sheet.
YOUNG is printed in a narrow street running north from E Liberty to the edge of the sheet.
OSM Betton runs along the north building line of the 1904 Clinton (houses 722-712). Red Clinton is correctly centred ~7-8 m south.
The Brighton Place diagonal cuts through buildings 2190/2188 and the canal tow-path strip.

This is the alley east of Colerain, continuing the red 'Brighton' (printed BRIGHTON west of Colerain). OSM runs ~2-3 m north of the band, and no name is printed east of Colerain. The nearby '10' belongs to the N-S Bright Alley.
